lead: The Verdi beard is a full beard kept short and shaped, with a rounded outline and trimmed edges, usually with the moustache integrated into it. It is named after the Italian composer Giuseppe Verdi, who wore a full beard in later life. People use a beard like this to frame the jaw and lower face.

Wikipedia notes that by the end of the 20th century the closely clipped Verdi beard, often with an integrated moustache, had become relatively common. No studies are listed that test this specific style.

paras: The beard is grown out and then maintained with trimming and shaping so that the outline stays rounded and the length even, often with the cheek line and neckline kept clean. Maintenance is the main routine.
Risks are those of shaving and trimming, such as razor irritation and ingrown hairs, and patchy beard growth may limit the look. Results depend on hair growth and face shape.

angle.text: A shaped full beard changes the visible outline of the lower face. Rounded, clipped edges are used to define the jaw and join the moustache into one shape.

lead: The Verdi beard is a style of full beard that is closely clipped, with a rounded shape and tidy edges, often paired with a matching integrated moustache. Wikipedia's Beard article uses the term for this closely clipped beard and says it had become relatively common by the end of the 20th century [1].

The name refers to the composer Giuseppe Verdi (1813-1901), one of the cultural figures the same article lists among those who adopted beards after the revolutions of 1848 [1][2]. The wiki's entry describes the shape as rounded with trimmed edges.

For looks, the idea is that an even beard with a defined outline frames the jaw and lower face and can add the impression of a fuller jawline. No published study examines the Verdi beard specifically.

paras: Beards became much more popular after the revolutions of 1848, when monarchs, statesmen and artists adopted them, Verdi among them [1]. Photographs of Verdi in his later years appear in his biography, including a c. 1872 portrait [2]. The closely clipped form carrying his name had become relatively common by the late 20th century [1].

timeline.event: After the revolutions of 1848 beards become widely fashionable among public figures, including Verdi [1].
A portrait of Verdi from this period appears in his biography [2].
The closely clipped Verdi beard, often with an integrated moustache, becomes relatively common [1].
